name: Domain-Driven Design
answer: A design approach for finding module or service boundaries around business areas. It's not a style; it supports modular monoliths and microservices.

name: Micro-frontends
answer: Splitting one web frontend so several teams can own and deploy parts of it. Worth it only when several teams share one large frontend; otherwise it adds complexity.

name: Client–server / two-tier
answer: A classic style: clients talk to one server. Mostly covered here by layered architecture (one server plus clients).

name: Actor model
answer: A concurrency model where actors keep their own state and talk by messages. It can implement event-driven or space-like systems; useful for highly concurrent, stateful work.

name: Blackboard
answer: A rare classic style where specialist components cooperate through a shared data store (used in some AI and speech systems). Closest here: event-driven.

name: Lambda / Kappa architecture
answer: Data-processing architectures for analytics (batch plus stream, or stream only). They're out of scope here: we rank application styles, not analytics platforms.

name: Data lake / lakehouse / data mesh
answer: Data architectures for analytics and reporting. Out of scope here; they sit beside whichever application style you choose.

name: LLM / RAG / agentic AI apps
answer: AI features are components, not a style: they can sit inside any style. Plan for slow or failing responses, cost and swapping providers.

name: Kubernetes / Docker
answer: Container platforms for deploying and scaling software. They're deployment technology, not an architectural style; commonly used with microservices or service-based.

name: MERN / MEAN / Spring / .NET
answer: These are technology stacks, not architectural styles. Any of them can implement most styles; choose the style first, then the stack.

name: Multi-tenant SaaS
answer: A system characteristic, not a style. If failures must be limited to some tenants, tick "Failures must only affect a subset of customers".

name: Mobile backend
answer: A system characteristic, not a style. Managed backends (BaaS) map to serverless; offline-first apps may point to edge or peer-to-peer.

name: Offline-first
answer: A system characteristic: the app keeps working without a network and syncs later. See the edge and peer-to-peer options in step 3.
